reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a BitConnect tutorial that invites viewers to invest $100, transfer Bitcoin into an account, and lend funds through the platform. It pairs this solicitation with claims of daily guaranteed interest and a projected 234% return, while also promoting multilevel referral earnings and directing viewers to get started. The interface connects investment with wallet payment and lending controls, although the available video evidence does not establish whether returns were realized, funds were recovered, or viewers experienced losses.

citations.quote: we are doing a BitConnect tutorial so you can learn all about BitConnect and how to do your first $100 investment
It's a platform that allows you to earn Bitcoin by lending Bitcoin.

we're going to deposit our bitcoins from our bitcoin wallet into our Bitconnect account, and secondly we will buy the Bitconnect coins or tokens as they're often referred to and we will purchase them from the BCC exchange and, thirdly, we're going to lend or invest our BitConnect coinsins in BitConnect lending platform
if you're lending between $100 and $1000, you will earn an average of 0.9% daily. And you can retrieve your capital investment within 299 days.
Any interest you earn can be cashed out immediately or you can reinvest it and keep making money, keep earning your interest.

opening.argument: The video presents information with meaningful qualifications rather than an unconditional promise. The speaker explicitly separates herself from the platform's wording, saying, "It's not my platform." She describes the earnings figures as approximate and explains that the calculator excludes compounded interest, so the projections are presented as estimates with limitations, not guaranteed outcomes. The material therefore supports informed evaluation of a platform's own claims rather than deceptive certainty.

citations.quote: I'm reading this sentence. It's not my platform.
That's an approximate amount. It could be more.
Keep in mind that this does not calculate compounded interest. This is on only one investment.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats every platform statement as the speaker's own solicitation, but the speaker expressly distinguishes herself from at least one platform claim. It also characterizes calculator outputs as promised returns even though the video calls the figures approximate and identifies an important limitation. Showing a possible investment workflow does not establish that the speaker guaranteed results or concealed uncertainty.

citations.quote: I'm reading this sentence. It's not my platform.
That's an approximate amount. It could be more.
Keep in mind that this does not calculate compounded interest. This is on only one investment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualifications do not undo the video's affirmative promotion. The speaker still says viewers can make a first $100 investment, earn daily interest, and cash out or reinvest it. Calling a projection approximate addresses mathematical precision, not whether the underlying investment opportunity is reliable or whether viewers should fund it.

if you're lending between $100 and $1000, you will earn an average of 0.9% daily.

opening.argument: The primary format is an operational tutorial. The title calls it a "Complete Bitconnect Tutorial," and the speaker says the purpose is to help viewers learn about the platform and complete a first investment. She then walks through account navigation, exchange functions, wallet transfers, and lending steps. Demonstrating how a website works is not itself proof of deceptive intent; the video can be understood as technology and financial-platform instruction, allowing viewers to inspect the process for themselves.

there are four steps and you can follow along with me on the screen here as you see

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening turns instructional detail into a solicitation without accounting for the video's stated tutorial purpose. The speaker repeatedly explains what appears on the screen and how the interface operates, including where to find the exchange and dashboard. Instruction can describe an investment process without establishing that the creator is making a knowingly false representation about the service.

citations.quote: Complete Bitconnect Tutorial - Angela Loves Crypto -
there are four steps and you can follow along with me on the screen here as you see
if you click on BCC exchange in the menu, it will take us through the exchange page

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing is not neutral when the instructions tell viewers to deposit Bitcoin, buy tokens, lend them, and watch earnings grow. The walkthrough is paired with enthusiastic claims about making money and a direction to get started, so the operational format functions as promotion rather than merely an objective demonstration.

opening.argument: The material can be read as a review and promotion of a cryptocurrency service with several ordinary platform functions: exchange, wallet management, lending, staking, trading, mining, and referrals. The supplied material shows interfaces and instructions, but it does not establish that a transfer was completed, that a viewer lost money, or that any particular return was actually realized. A displayed account control and a projected calculator are evidence of advertised functionality, not proof of a scam mechanism or an outcome.

citations.quote: There are several different opportunities and ways that you can earn with bitconnect
We're going to transfer Bitcoin to BCC and we we'll do that here into BCC exchange
the projected earnings calculator on the far right corner of the screen

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of ordinary wallet and exchange controls does not prove the service is legitimate, but it does leave the alleged mechanism incomplete. The available evidence does not establish an actual completed investment, recovered or unrecovered funds, or realized returns. A referral feature can also exist in ordinary promotions; its presence alone does not establish deceptive recruitment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-loss evidence is not required to classify the promotion. The video expressly instructs viewers to deposit Bitcoin, buy BCC, and lend it, while advertising daily interest and referral percentages. The referral system is described as earnings from multiple levels, so the evidence shows more than an ordinary purchase or a merely displayed interface.
